Every version of a document, oldest first, the current one last.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.DocStore.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### *class* annals.LocalTarget(root)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A directory on this machine.

`read_metas()` keeps each meta it parsed, keyed by its file’s inode, mtime, ctime
and size (every write replaces the file, so a new inode), and resolves the root once
per listing, not twice per file: listing a thousand documents costs a `stat` per

### annals.configure(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, outbox=False, share_base_url=None, room=False)

Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.

### Example

`annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals`.
`--to NAME` saves the target and base url as a named target (`annals publish --to NAME`)
and leaves the default alone. `--outbox` marks the target as an outbox: a directory
the server pulls and empties (it cannot be written to from here), so replacements are
left for the server to apply; it is kept by later changes (`ANNALS_OUTBOX=0` or an
edit of the file turns it off). `--share-base-url` is where share links point when
the share server is not at `<base-url>/shared` (a platform running it as its own
public app). `--room` marks a target an outside audience reads (a client’s room): what
is published or copied to it carries no provenance; kept by later changes, like
`--outbox`. With no arguments, shows the resolved settings without writing.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.group(title, doc_ids, , add_to=None, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.

With `add_to` (a group id) the documents are added to that group instead, and `title`
is ignored. The documents must exist and not be in the bin; the title is cleaned (see
[`annals.store.clean_title()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.clean_title)).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

`to` names a `[targets.NAME]` table of the config file; it replaces the environment
and the file’s default target for this call (explicit arguments still win).

* **Return type:**
  [`Settings`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.Settings)

### annals.ls(q='', , trash=False, limit=50, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, since=None, session=None, tag=None, meta=None)

List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.

`to` lists a named target instead of the default one. The rest are exact filters,
all of which must hold, for tools that poll: `since` (an ISO date or time, or an age
like `6h` or `2d`: published or replaced at or after it), `session` (the publishing session’s
name, whole, case-sensitive), `tag` (one tag, whole: the owner’s own tags, set by `annals tag`, win over the publisher’s) and `meta` (`key=value`,
several allowed, against the document’s `source`: `corpus=annals`). A row is
`{id, title, kind, tags, created, updated, source, url}`; with `--json` that is the contract
(`misc/docs/design.md`), and `total` counts the matches before `limit`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.parse_target(spec)

`host:/path` becomes an [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.SshTarget); anything else a [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.LocalTarget).

* **Return type:**
  [`Target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target)

### annals.publish(paths, , title=None, tags='', group=None, add_to=None, session=None, session_url=None, all_files=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, replace=None, artifact=None, no_link_check=False, no_pdf=False, meta=None)

Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.

An audio or video file takes its timed text along as one document: `talk.mp3
talk.vtt talk.chapters.vtt` (or `talk.cues.json`) is one audio document whose page
shows the transcript and chapters (`annals.store.SIDECAR_SUFFIXES`).

`paths`: files of any kind (markdown, html, images, video, audio, pdf, text), a
directory (one document: an `index.html` or single page with its assets, else a
gallery of everything in it), or `-` for stdin (markdown). `tags` is comma separated. `group`
names a group to create from the published documents; the reply then carries
`group_url` too. `add_to` appends them to an existing group instead (its id, as
printed in a group link), so a second batch lands under the link the owner already has. `session` records who published (the source shown on the page), and `session_url`
the claude.ai link that opens that session; by default the link of the Claude Code session
this runs in (`CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`), `none` for no link. The document’s page
shows each session that made it, linked, under its title; a share or a room never does
([`annals.sessions`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#module-annals.sessions)). A directory skips
hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`) unless `all_files`.
`to` publishes to a named target of the config file (`[targets.NAME]`, see
`annals configure --to`) instead of the default one. `replace` (a document’s link or
id) publishes ONE path as a new version of that document: the link stays the same, the
page shows the new version and offers the earlier ones. That is how a living page (a
guide, a status page) keeps one link. `artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive
version” button. Publish the Artifact first, then the same page here with its link.
A markdown or text document that mentions an issue or a Slack/email/chat message
without linking to it gets a warning on stderr ([`annals.linkcheck`](_autosummary/annals.linkcheck.html.md#module-annals.linkcheck)); it is
published either way. `no_link_check` turns that check off.

An html page gets its own Download PDF button, inside the page, so it survives “open
full page”, raw links and shares, and `<stem>.pdf` printed beside it (headless
Chromium, the `pdf` extra; without it the button opens the print dialog). A page that
already has its PDF says so with `<link rel="alternate" type="application/pdf"
href="...">`; one with its own button marks it `data-annals-pdf`; `no_pdf` (or
`data-annals-pdf="off"` on `<html>`/`<body>`) leaves the page as it is
([`annals.pagepdf`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#module-annals.pagepdf)).

`meta` (`--meta key=value [key=value ...]`) records what the document belongs to, next
to `host`, `cwd` and `session` in its `source`: by convention `corpus` (the
repository or body of work), `repo`, `issue` (the issue it answers), `item` (a
desk item) and `kind` (report, brief, overview, render); other keys are kept as given.
`ls --session/--meta` finds them again. The CLI’s `--json` prints the result below
(`id`, `title`, `url`, and with a group `group_id` and `group_url`; several
paths give `docs`) as JSON and nothing else on stdout; that shape is a contract
(`misc/docs/design.md`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.restore(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Bring documents back from the recycle bin.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.show(doc_id, , target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

A document’s metadata, link, the groups it is in, and the annals links in its text.

`doc_id` may be the document’s link, on any annals this machine is configured for: the
link finds its own place (`to` names one explicitly). A group’s link gives the group
and its documents’ links. `links` are the links to other annals documents and groups
found in the document’s text files, on any annals this machine can read: follow them
with `annals show` or `annals aggregate`. To read the text, use `annals aggregate <link>`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.trash(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md

# annals.jsonstore

A `MutableMapping` kept in one JSON file, safe with several server processes.

The owner’s tags ([`annals.tags`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#module-annals.tags)) and each reader’s listening progress
([`annals.listening`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#module-annals.listening)) are small, server-side records that the page changes one entry at
a time. [`JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore) is that one mechanism: a JSON object in a file, written
atomically under an exclusive `flock`, re-read whenever another process changed it, and
never broken by a damaged file (it reads as empty and is kept aside at the next write).

A subclass says what a valid value is ([`JsonFileStore.valid()`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore.valid)) and how a value is
cleaned before it is stored ([`JsonFileStore.clean()`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore.clean)). [`JsonFileStore.modify()`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore.modify)
changes one entry from its current value under the lock, so two devices reporting at once
never lose each other’s change.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> s = JsonFileStore(pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "x.json")
>>> s["a"] = {"n": 1}
>>> s.modify("a", lambda v: {"n": (v or {}).get("n", 0) + 1})
{'n': 2}
>>> dict(s)
{'a': {'n': 2}}
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DAMAGED_SUFFIX`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.DAMAGED_SUFFIX)   | the suffix a damaged file is kept under, so a hand edit gone wrong can be recovered   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore)(path)   | `{key: value}` in one JSON file, re-read when another process changed it.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### annals.jsonstore.DAMAGED_SUFFIX *= '.damaged'*

the suffix a damaged file is kept under, so a hand edit gone wrong can be recovered

### *class* annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore(path)

Bases: [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

`{key: value}` in one JSON file, re-read when another process changed it.

A write takes an exclusive `flock` on `<file>.lock`, re-reads the file, changes it
and replaces it atomically. A read re-reads the file whenever its inode, size or mtime
changed (every write makes a new inode). `label` names the store in log messages.

#### clean(value)

The value as stored; raise `ValueError` to refuse it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### modify(key, change)

Set `key` to `change(current value or None)`, atomically; returns the stored value.

`change` returning `None` deletes the entry (and returns `None`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### snapshot()

Every entry at once, under one read (what a listing overlays).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### valid(value)

Whether a value read from the file is kept (an invalid one is logged and skipped).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/annals.linkcheck.html.md

# annals.linkcheck

Find what a document mentions without linking to it: the owner reads on a phone and clicks through.

A published report says “Karl asked on 10-29 in #tech-app-test” or “see owner/repo#12”.
Without a link the reader has to go and find the message or the issue, often on a phone.
This module finds such mentions so `annals publish` can warn the author. It only warns
and never blocks: the author decides.

Two kinds, both in markdown or plain text (code spans and fenced blocks are ignored):

- `issue`: a GitHub-style reference, `owner/repo#12` or a bare `#12`, outside a link;
- `message`: a line that points at one message (a message, a thread, a DM, a reply, a
  post, someone who asked, said or wrote, or a `#channel`) tied to a date,
  and has no web address at all. A dated pointer to a conversation names one message, so it should be
  its permalink. Headings and date ranges (“2026-10-04 → 2026-11-07”) are periods, not
  messages, and are skipped.

```pycon
>>> doc = '''# Catch-up
... - Karl asked on 2026-10-29 in #tech-app-test what was missing.
... - Karl asked on [2026-10-29](https://x.slack.com/archives/C1/p1) in #tech-app-test.
... - Tracked in inoocq/meta#7 and #12.
... - Tracked in [inoocq/meta#7](https://github.com/inoocq/meta/issues/7).
... - Run `git log #3` here.
... ## Slack, 2026-10-04 → 2026-11-07
... - 574 messages from 2026-10-04 to 2026-11-07, Slack read by hand until 10-04.
... '''
>>> [(m.line, m.kind, m.ref) for m in unlinked_mentions(doc)]
[(2, 'message', 'Slack/chat message of 2026-10-29'), (4, 'issue', 'inoocq/meta#7'), (4, 'issue', '#12')]
```

Ordinary prose is not flagged: a colour, a date that is not tied to the conversation word, a
table row.

```pycon
>>> prose = '''A base surface of #121212 and #0b0b12.
... The composition review of 2026-11-12 [19] found that the owner's reply reaches an agent.
... | library | archived, last push 2026-09-18 | can post to a URL |
... Released 2026-05-01; its documentation said nothing about this.
... '''
>>> unlinked_mentions(prose)
[]
```

# _autosummary/annals.listening.html.md

# annals.listening

What each reader has heard of each audio document: percent heard, listens, where they stopped.

The page reports what was played, a few seconds at a time, as spans of the audio’s own
timeline (`[[start, end], ...]` in seconds). The server keeps the **union** of those spans
per reader and document, so the percent heard counts each second once, however often it was
replayed or skipped back to, and two devices reporting the same minute add nothing twice.
A listen is counted when playback reaches the end of audio that has been heard almost
whole ([`DONE_SHARE`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.DONE_SHARE)), so dragging to the end is not a listen; a report carries the
id of the play it belongs to, so a report sent twice (a retry, a page closing) counts one.

A record, per reader and document:

```default
{"heard": [[0.0, 61.5], [90.0, 120.0]], "duration": 300.0, "position": 120.0,
 "listens": 1, "done": true, "updated": "2026-11-09T10:00:00+00:00"}
```

`done` is the reader’s own mark (“I have heard this”), set or cleared from the page; it
is absent until they set it. [`status()`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.status) reads a record as one of [`STATUSES`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.STATUSES).

Records live under the data root, one JSON file per reader (`listening/<reader>.json`),
through [`annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore). [`for_reader()`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.for_reader) is the seam: any
`(reader) -> store` callable whose stores are [`Records`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.Records) can replace it
(`mk_api(listening=...)`).

```pycon
>>> merge_spans([[5, 10], [0, 3], [2, 6], [20, 20]])
[[0.0, 10.0]]
>>> rec = apply_report(None, {"spans": [[0, 30]], "duration": 100, "position": 30})
>>> percent(rec), status(rec)
(30, 'started')
>>> apply_report(None, {"spans": [[95, 100]], "duration": 100, "ended": "p0"})["listens"]  # dragged to the end
0
>>> rec = apply_report(rec, {"spans": [[30, 100]], "duration": 100, "position": 100, "ended": "p1"})
>>> rec = apply_report(rec, {"spans": [], "duration": 100, "position": 100, "ended": "p1"})
>>> percent(rec), rec["listens"], status(rec)
(100, 1, 'done')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`STATUSES`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.STATUSES)         | what a record reads as, in the order the page offers them as filters               |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DONE_SHARE`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.DONE_SHARE)       | heard at least this share of the audio counts as done, without a listen to the end |
| [`MIN_STARTED_S`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.MIN_STARTED_S)    | heard less than this many seconds is not started (a stray tap on play)             |

# _autosummary/annals.mcp.html.md

# annals.mcp

MCP surface: the same operations as the CLI, from [`annals.tools`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#module-annals.tools), via `py2mcp`.

Run with `python -m annals.mcp` (needs `pip install 'annals[mcp]'`). String refs keep the
core free of any MCP import; the function list is the CLI’s (`annals.tools.EFFECTS` classifies
each operation), narrowed to the effects the host allows: by default read and write, not the
destructive `purge` or `listen`, which spends money.

### Module Attributes

| [`ENV_EFFECTS`](_autosummary/annals.mcp.html.md#annals.mcp.ENV_EFFECTS)   | the environment variable that widens (or narrows) what the server offers   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`mk_server`](_autosummary/annals.mcp.html.md#annals.mcp.mk_server)(\*[, effects])   | Build the MCP server over [`annals.tools`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#module-annals.tools).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### annals.mcp.ENV_EFFECTS *= 'ANNALS_MCP_EFFECTS'*

the environment variable that widens (or narrows) what the server offers

### annals.mcp.mk_server(, effects=None)

Build the MCP server over [`annals.tools`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#module-annals.tools).

`effects` (default `read` and `write`, or the comma separated `ANNALS_MCP_EFFECTS`)
says which operations to serve; `destructive` adds `purge`, `spend` adds `listen`
(it costs money), `file` adds `aggregate --output`.


# _autosummary/annals.media.html.md

# annals.media

The media relay for published html pages: what a framed page plays, told to the page around it.

A spoken overview is an html page shown in a sandboxed frame, so the annals page cannot see
its audio. This adds one inlined script (the page’s own `ui/media-progress.js`) to any
html page that may play audio or video; the script posts what is played to the parent
page, which records what the reader heard ([`annals.listening`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#module-annals.listening)), and takes a “start at”
from it. Opened on its own (no parent), the script does nothing.

### Functions

| [`add_media_relay`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.add_media_relay)(html)   | `html` with the media relay injected, unless it plays nothing or opts out.                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`media_version`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.media_version)()         | A short hash of what [`add_media_relay()`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.add_media_relay) injects, for a page's ETag. |

### annals.media.add_media_relay(html)

`html` with the media relay injected, unless it plays nothing or opts out.

```pycon
>>> add_media_relay(b"<p>no media</p>") == b"<p>no media</p>"
True
>>> b"annalsMedia" in add_media_relay(b"<body><audio src=a.mp3></audio></body>")
True
>>> add_media_relay(b"<p>an audio overview</p>") == b"<p>an audio overview</p>"
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### annals.media.media_version()

A short hash of what [`add_media_relay()`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.add_media_relay) injects, for a page’s ETag.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md

# annals.notebook

A share’s documents as separate notebook sources: one plain web page per text file.

A notebook product (NotebookLM, and Gemini’s notebooks, which share its sources) takes a
web page by its link, one source per link, and several links pasted at once; it reads
the page’s text and keeps its own copy. It does not unpack a zip, and its upload picker
needs the files on the device first. So the fewest taps from an iPad is: tick the
documents, copy one list of links, paste it into the notebook (see
`misc/docs/notebook-sources.md` for the research behind this).

The links are a share’s ([`annals.share`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#module-annals.share)): unguessable, scoped to the documents
ticked, expiring, revocable, and filtered like every shared text. This module only
decides what becomes a source and how one looks:

```default
GET <share link>/source/<doc id>/<file>   a script-free html page: <title>, the text
```

- [`source_files()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_files): which files of a document are sources (markdown and html pages,
  numbered files first, as [`annals.aggregate.numbered_first()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.numbered_first) orders them).
- [`notebook_sources()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.notebook_sources): the `{doc, file, title, url}` rows of a share, in its order.
- [`source_scope()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_scope): what a notebook share includes of a document: its source pages
  and the files they show, never the rest of a folder.
- [`render_source()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.render_source): one markdown file as its source page ([`render_source_body()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.render_source_body)
  is the page’s body alone, which the share page embeds), shared-text rules applied
  twice: to the text ([`annals.share.filter_refs()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.filter_refs)), then to every link and image of
  the rendered page ([`annals.share.ref_decider()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.ref_decider) over markdown-it’s tokens), and
  any annals id left in it removed. Cached, and rendered only up to
  [`RENDER_MAX_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.RENDER_MAX_BYTES) (a larger file is sent as escaped text): it is a public route.
- [`source_page()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_page): the page a notebook reads. Its `<title>` is the document’s title,
  which the notebook shows as the source’s name, so the sources can be told apart.
- [`markdown_html()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.markdown_html): markdown to html; `markdown-it-py` when installed (the
  `pdf` extra), else the text escaped in a `<pre>`, which a notebook reads as well.

# _autosummary/annals.overview.html.md

# annals.overview

Spoken overviews of a document: the request a page makes, and the worker that fulfils it.

A reader asks for an overview from a document’s page. That writes one small JSON file under
the data root (`overviews/<doc id>.json`). A worker on the same machine reads the document
from the store, runs a command that makes the overview, and publishes the result as a
document of its own. The page polls the request’s state.

annals does not know how an overview is made. The command is the seam: any program that
takes a text file and writes one HTML page, named in `ANNALS_OVERVIEW_COMMAND` or passed to
[`work()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.work), with `{source}`, `{minutes}` and `{out}` filled in, and `{url}`, the source document’s
page, so the overview can link to what it was based on:

```default
my-overview {source} --minutes {minutes} --player-to {out} --source-url {url}
```

The feature is off unless the host turns it on (`mk_api(overviews=True)`), because making
an overview spends money. A host can also offer it to some readers only
(`mk_api(overviews={"me@example.com"})`, or `ANNALS_OVERVIEWS` for `annals.api.mk_app()`;
see [`readers_offered()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.readers_offered)): the others get no Listen button, and the documents the feature
makes ([`made_here()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.made_here)) are hidden from them. For the same reason, a current overview is not made again unless
forced, a crash after publishing does not pay twice, `work` stops at a daily limit, and a
request nobody fulfilled expires rather than spending money whenever a worker next wakes.

Run the worker on a timer. Finished request files stay in the folder and the worker writes
there, so a watcher on the folder would keep waking it.

When the command cannot work until someone acts (an expired login, a voice account out of
credit), pressing again only spends the daily limit. So the worker notices it: the same
failure, fast, from two documents in a row, marks the maker *down* with that reason (a
document failing twice is that document). An agent can mark it too, with a link to where it
is being fixed (`annals listen-down "why" --link URL`). While it is down, nothing fails or
is dropped: requests *wait* (past the daily limit too), the page says why and what to do
instead of offering a Try again, and the worker tries one of them again every few hours. The
first success, or `annals listen-down --clear`, clears the mark and queues everything that
waited.

```pycon
>>> html_to_text("<title>x</title><p>One &amp; two</p><script>no()</script><p>Three</p>")
'One & two\n\nThree'
>>> [c["characters"] for c in choices()]
[2700, 4500, 6300]
```

### annals.overview.readers_offered(spec)

Who may ask for and hear overviews: `False` (nobody), `True` (every reader), or a test.

`spec` is what a host passes as `overviews`: a bool, a predicate on the reader’s name
(an email, as `annals.api.reader_of()` gives it), a collection of names, or a string as
`ANNALS_OVERVIEWS` holds it (names separated by commas, `*` for every reader, empty for
nobody; `true`/`1`/`yes` and `false`/`0`/`no` mean the same as `*` and empty,
never a reader so named). Names are compared without case.

```pycon
>>> readers_offered("*"), readers_offered(""), readers_offered(None)
(True, False, False)
>>> readers_offered("true"), readers_offered(" No "), readers_offered(["*"])
(True, False, True)
>>> may = readers_offered(" Me@Example.com, ")
>>> may("me@example.com"), may("someone@example.com")
(True, False)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]

### annals.overview.request(store, requests, doc_id, , minutes=5, force=False)

Ask for an overview of a document. Raises `ValueError` if it cannot be asked for.

Asking again while one is being made changes nothing, and neither does asking for one
that exists and is current unless `force`, so a repeat costs nothing. While the maker
is down ([`maker_down()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.maker_down)), the request waits for it rather than failing.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.overview.request_combined(store, requests, docs, , title, group=None, minutes=5, max_bytes=None)

Ask for ONE overview of several documents: of the document combining their text.

Nothing is published here. When the documents were combined before, that document gets
an ordinary request. Otherwise the request is queued, with the document ids, under
[`combined_request_id()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.combined_request_id) (a record marked `kind: "combine"`), and the worker makes
the combined document (see [`combined_document()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.combined_document)) when it starts the job, so a
request nobody works leaves no document behind. Returns `{"doc": <combined document
id, or None until the worker has made it>, "listen": <the overview's state>}`. Raises
`ValueError` as [`request()`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.request) does, or when there is nothing to speak or too much
of it: refused now, not after the request has waited for a worker.

The key names the documents at their versions *now*. A retry after one of them changed
is a different key, so a new request: the old failed one stays listed until it expires.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.overview.state_of(store, requests, meta)

What a page shows for a document: its request’s state and what it can start.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.overview.unmade(store, requests)

The overviews asked for and not (yet) made: being made, waiting, or failed recently.

Each is `state_of` its document plus `doc`, `title`, `created` (the document’s),
`requested` and `finished` (the last try’s). A queued combination of several documents
has no document yet: `doc` is `None` and `combine` has the `docs` and `group`
to ask again with (`POST /overviews`). A request whose document is gone, binned
or no longer speakable is left out: nothing can be retried. Newest first.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### annals.overview.valid_minutes(minutes)

Whether this is a length on offer. Exactly an int: not `True`, and not `3.0`.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### annals.overview.work(store, requests, \*, command=None, timeout=1800, daily_limit=None, doc_url=<class 'str'>)

Fulfil every queued request, one at a time, until none is left; return what happened.

A failure is recorded on its request, for the page to show, and the next one still runs.
A request made while this runs is picked up before it exits. `doc_url` turns a document
id into its page, for `{url}`. While the maker is down, requests wait, and one of them
is tried every [`PROBE_EVERY_S`](_autosummary/annals.overview.html.md#annals.overview.PROBE_EVERY_S); once one works, those waiting run too.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]


# _autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md

# annals.pagepdf

Every published html page carries its own Download PDF button, and the PDF beside it.

A page is often read without the annals page around it: opened full page, its raw url
mailed on, or shared. So at publish time the stored html itself gets a small “Download
PDF” link (hidden when printing), pointing at `<stem>.pdf` in the same document:

1. **The page opts out** (`data-annals-pdf="off"` on `<html>` or `<body>`, or
   `annals publish --no-pdf`): nothing is added.
2. **The page has its own button** (any element with `data-annals-pdf`): nothing is
   added; it already says where its PDF is.
3. **The page declares its PDF** (`<link rel="alternate" type="application/pdf"
   href="...">`): the button points there, and nothing is printed.
4. **The document already holds** `<stem>.pdf` beside the page: the button points at it.
5. **Otherwise the page is printed** to `<stem>.pdf` by `pdf_renderer` (default
   [`print_with_chromium()`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.print_with_chromium), pdfdol’s headless Chromium, in the `pdf` extra). When it
   > cannot print (no Chromium, a page that will not load in time), the button calls the
   > browser’s own print dialog instead, so it is never missing.

What this adds is one block wrapped in `<!--annals-pdf-->` markers (pure ASCII, so it
suits a page in any charset), so publishing a page that already went through here (a new
version through `--replace`) swaps the old button for a new one and prints the new page
again. The page’s bytes are otherwise kept as they were, whatever their encoding.

### Module Attributes

| [`PdfRenderer`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.PdfRenderer)                            | `path of a staged html page -> PDF bytes`; raises when it cannot print                                                                                          |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_PRINT_TIMEOUT_S`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.DFLT_PRINT_TIMEOUT_S)                   | the longest a page may take to print, in seconds, before the button prints instead                                                                              |
| [`DFLT_PDF_RENDERER`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.DFLT_PDF_RENDERER)(page, \*[, timeout]) | what [`attach_pdf()`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.attach_pdf) prints with when not told; read at call time, so a test or an embedding app can swap it once |
| [`DFLT`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.DFLT)                                   | "the default renderer", told apart from `None` (never print)                                                                                                    |

`path of a staged html page -> PDF bytes`; raises when it cannot print

alias of [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)], [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]

### annals.pagepdf.add_button(page, href)

`page` with a Download PDF link to `href` (or a print button when `None`).

One block goes right after `<body>` (or where the body would start): a `<link
rel="alternate">` declaring the PDF, so readers and agents find it, its style, and
the button. Any button added earlier is replaced. `href` is used as given (quote a
file name first: [`attach_pdf()`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.attach_pdf) does).

```pycon
>>> page = "<!doctype html><html><head></head><body><p>x</p></body></html>"
>>> out = add_button(page, "x.pdf")
>>> 'href="x.pdf"' in out and 'type="application/pdf"' in out
True
>>> out.startswith("<!doctype html>")
True
>>> "window.print()" in add_button("<p>x</p>", None)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.pagepdf.attach_pdf(root, main, files, , pdf_renderer='default')

Give the staged html page `root/main` its PDF button (and its PDF).

Returns `(files, pdf)`: `files` (relative to `root`) gains `<stem>.pdf` when it
is printed here, and `pdf` is where the page’s PDF is (a file of the document, or
the url the page declared), `None` when there is none. `pdf_renderer` defaults to
[`DFLT_PDF_RENDERER`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.DFLT_PDF_RENDERER); `None` never prints: the button links to a PDF the
document or the page already has, else opens the print dialog. A renderer that fails
is logged and treated the same way; publishing never fails for want of a PDF.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### annals.pagepdf.button_href(page)

Where the button annals put in `page` points (`None`: none, or a print button).

```pycon
>>> button_href(add_button("<p>x</p>", "x.pdf"))
'x.pdf'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### annals.pagepdf.declared_pdf(page)

The href of the page’s own `<link rel="alternate" type="application/pdf">`.

A link annals added itself does not count: that is not the page declaring one.

```pycon
>>> declared_pdf('<link rel="alternate" type="application/pdf" href="guide.pdf">')
'guide.pdf'
>>> declared_pdf('<link rel="stylesheet" href="a.css">') is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### annals.pagepdf.print_with_chromium(page, , timeout=60)

Print an html file to PDF with headless Chromium (pdfdol), with its print css.

Needs the `pdf` extra and `playwright install chromium`. It runs in a child
process, killed (with its browser) after `timeout` seconds. Images marked
`loading="lazy"` would print blank, so the page is printed from a copy without
that attribute, beside it so its relative files still load.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### annals.pagepdf.strip_button(page)

`page` without what [`add_button()`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#annals.pagepdf.add_button) put in it.

```pycon
>>> strip_button(add_button("<body><p>x</p></body>", "x.pdf"))
'<body><p>x</p></body>'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.pagepdf.wants_button(page)

False when the page opts out, or already has a PDF button of its own.

```pycon
>>> wants_button("<p>plain</p>")
True
>>> wants_button('<body data-annals-pdf="off"><p>x</p></body>')
False
>>> wants_button('<a href="g.pdf" data-annals-pdf>PDF</a>')
False
>>> wants_button('<script>"<a data-annals-pdf>"</script><p data-annals-pdf-note=1>')
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/annals.records.html.md

# annals.records

The published documents as records for a retrieval index, so an agent can find one by meaning.

annals keeps its own full-text index for the page’s search box ([`annals.search`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#module-annals.search)).
Searching by meaning (“the report comparing local TTS engines”) is `ir`’s job, and `ir`
takes any package’s records through a named callable: register this one once (from Python;
`ir register` on the command line has no records option) and `ir` rebuilds from it:

```default
import ir, annals.records
ir.register("annals", "records", fetcher="annals.records:records",
            metadata_keys=list(annals.records.METADATA_KEYS))
ir.build_corpus("annals")       # then: ir discover annals "the report comparing local TTS engines"
```

One record per current document (the bin and earlier versions are not indexed). A markdown,
text or html document brings its text (html without its markup); a folder or a document of
several markdown files brings them as one text, as `annals aggregate` makes it; any other
kind (an image, a PDF) brings its title and excerpt, so it can still be found. Overviews and
combined documents duplicate their sources, so they are left out unless asked for. A document
the owner or the publisher tagged `noindex` or `private` (any case) is never yielded.

Run it where the documents are: it refuses an outbox and a remote target, because the
owner’s tags (the privacy gate) live beside the documents, and an index built from a partial
view would drop the rest. Two things belong to the index, not to this function: `ir` decides
a record changed by hashing its `text`, so a retag or retitle reaches the index’s filters
only on a rebuild that is `full` (which also prunes a document trashed, purged or newly
tagged `noindex`; register with full builds). `url` uses this machine’s `base_url`.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> from annals.store import DocStore
>>> root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> store = DocStore(root)
>>> _ = store.publish(text="# Local TTS engines\n\nPiper and Kokoro compared.", title="TTS", tags=["research"])
>>> _ = store.publish(text="# Secret\n\nnot for an index", title="S", tags=["noindex"])
>>> [(r["title"], r["tags"], "Kokoro" in r["text"]) for r in records(target=str(root))]
[('TTS', 'research', True)]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_SKIP_TAGS`](_autosummary/annals.records.html.md#annals.records.DFLT_SKIP_TAGS)   | a document with one of these tags (any case) is never indexed                     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DERIVED_TAGS`](_autosummary/annals.records.html.md#annals.records.DERIVED_TAGS)     | overviews and combined files                                                      |
| [`METADATA_KEYS`](_autosummary/annals.records.html.md#annals.records.METADATA_KEYS)    | the record fields that are filters in the index (`ir`'s `metadata_keys`)          |
| [`MAX_TEXT_CHARS`](_autosummary/annals.records.html.md#annals.records.MAX_TEXT_CHARS)   | a text is cut to this many characters, so one huge document cannot swamp an index |

### Functions

| [`records`](_autosummary/annals.records.html.md#annals.records.records)(\*[, target, to, skip_tags, ...])   | One dict per indexable document: `id`, `text` and the [`METADATA_KEYS`](_autosummary/annals.records.html.md#annals.records.METADATA_KEYS).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

* **Type:**
  the tags of documents made from other documents

### annals.records.DFLT_SKIP_TAGS *= frozenset({'noindex', 'private'})*

# _autosummary/annals.references.html.md

# annals.references

The references of documents, extracted and combined, in three forms.

A document’s references are the body of its references section: a markdown heading named
“References”, “Sources”, “Bibliography”, “Works cited” or “Citations” (any level, any case),
down to the next heading of the same or a higher level. Three forms, each text in, text out:

- `grouped` (the default): one `###` section per document holding its references as
  they are, under `## References for <title>`;
- `deduped`: every entry once, its citation number removed, as one bulleted list;
- `urls`: every web address once, one per line and nothing else, the form a notebook
  (Gemini Notebook, formerly NotebookLM) accepts as pasted website sources.

```pycon
>>> doc = '''# Bees
... Text [1].
... ## REFERENCES
... 1. [Hive life](https://bees.org/hive). 2024.
... [2] Smith J. Pollen, <https://pollen.net/a>
... ## Appendix
... not a reference https://no.org
... '''
>>> reference_sections(doc)
['1. [Hive life](https://bees.org/hive). 2024.\n[2] Smith J. Pollen, <https://pollen.net/a>']
>>> [strip_citation_number(e) for e in reference_entries(reference_sections(doc)[0])]
['[Hive life](https://bees.org/hive). 2024.', 'Smith J. Pollen, <https://pollen.net/a>']
>>> print(combine_references([("Bees", [doc]), ("Wasps", ["no references here"])],
...                          title="Insects", form="urls"), end="")
https://bees.org/hive
https://pollen.net/a
```

The mechanism knows nothing of the store: [`doc_reference_texts()`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.doc_reference_texts) is the bridge that
reads a set of documents through a `read(doc_id, rel)` callable, so the owner’s API and,
later, a share can use it alike.

### Module Attributes

| [`REFERENCE_HEADINGS`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.REFERENCE_HEADINGS)   | section names that hold references (a heading's text starts with one of them)   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`combine_references`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.combine_references)(items, \*, title[, form]) | `items` (a title and the texts of its pages) as their references in `form`.                  |
| [`doc_reference_texts`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.doc_reference_texts)(docs, \*, read[, skip])  | `(title, texts)` for each of `docs` (`(meta, files)` pairs): its markdown pages' text.       |
| [`reference_entries`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.reference_entries)(section)                   | The entries of a references section: each numbered or bulleted item, with its wrapped lines. |
| [`reference_sections`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.reference_sections)(text)                     | The body of each references section of a markdown text, as written (blank edges trimmed).    |
| [`strip_citation_number`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.strip_citation_number)(entry)                 | `entry` without its leading number or bullet (`1.`, `[1]`, `-`).                             |
| [`url_key`](_autosummary/annals.references.html.md#annals.references.url_key)(url)                                 | What makes two addresses the same page: no fragment, no trailing slash, host in lowercase.   |

`text` is empty when none had any. Every surface (the HTTP route, `annals references`,

# _autosummary/annals.render.html.md

# annals.render

Render markdown (and other page-like files) to html and PDF, with their images inside.

No web framework in here, so the CLI can use it as the server does. The PDF is made by
WeasyPrint from markdown-it’s HTML (raw html in the markdown is shown as text, never
interpreted). Images are embedded; audio, video, other PDFs and files become a visible link
to the resource, so the reader can open or play it. WeasyPrint is imported on first use; a
missing one is a [`annals.requirements.MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency) with the install hint.

Nothing is fetched from the network: an image outside the document is a link, never loaded.
Everything WeasyPrint is allowed to load is a placeholder url (`annals-file:N`) for bytes
this module already holds (`Embedded`).

### Module Attributes

| [`PDF_IMAGE_MAX_PX`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.PDF_IMAGE_MAX_PX)       | longest side of an embedded image; a 6000 px render is shrunk, a phone screenshot is not              |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`PDF_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.PDF_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES)    | an image larger than this on disk is linked, not embedded                                             |
| [`PDF_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.PDF_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS)   | an image with more pixels than this is not decoded to be shrunk (a small box would run out of memory) |
| [`PDF_IMAGES_TOTAL_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.PDF_IMAGES_TOTAL_BYTES) | all embedded images of one PDF together                                                               |
| [`PDF_MAX_TEXT_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.PDF_MAX_TEXT_BYTES)     | markdown larger than this is not made into a PDF (rendering cost grows faster than size)              |

### Functions

| [`html_to_pdf`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.html_to_pdf)(doc, embedder)                         | A4 PDF of the html page `doc`; the only things it may load are `embedder`'s.        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`inline_embedded`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.inline_embedded)(body, embedder)                    | `body` with each placeholder url replaced by a `data:` url of its bytes.            |
| `kind_of_mime`(rel)                                                                                 |                                                                                     |
| [`markdown_to_html`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.markdown_to_html)(text, \*, rel, files, ...[, ...]) | The html body of the markdown `text` (the file `rel` of a document) and its images. |
| [`markdown_to_pdf`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.markdown_to_pdf)(text, \*, title, rel, files, ...)  | A titled A4 PDF of the markdown `text` with its images inside (see the module doc). |
| [`page_html`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.page_html)(title, body, \*[, created, css, ...])    | A standalone html page: the `title` as the document title, then `body`.             |

### Classes

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Images the document holds are embedded (placeholder urls in the returned
[`Embedder`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.Embedder)); other files become links, shown as media rows; external images are
never fetched. Raw html in the markdown is text, not markup. `read_bytes(rel)` reads
an image the way the caller allows (a share filters svg text); `list_unreferenced=False`
leaves out the “More in this document” rows (when the document’s other files are
sections of a combined output of their own).

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Embedder`](_autosummary/annals.render.html.md#annals.render.Embedder)]

# _autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md

# annals.requirements

Optional dependencies, checked where they are needed and explained when they are missing.

annals installs light: a heavy library (WeasyPrint for PDFs, pypdf for joining them,
markdownify for html to markdown) is imported only when the conversion that needs it runs,
and a missing one is a [`MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency) that says which conversion needed it and
the exact command that fixes it, never a bare `ImportError` from deep inside a library.

```pycon
>>> check_requirements("json", what="anything")        # present: returns quietly
>>> try:
...     check_requirements("no_such_module_xyz", what="Combining into PDF")
... except MissingDependency as e:
...     print(str(e).splitlines()[0])
Combining into PDF needs no_such_module_xyz, which is not installed.
```

The pip name and the hint for a module are in [`PACKAGES`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.PACKAGES), so a new optional library is
one entry there.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_EXTRA`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.DFLT_EXTRA)   | the extra of annals that installs everything a conversion may need   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`PACKAGES`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.PACKAGES)     | module name -> (pip name, system hint or `""`)                       |

### Functions

| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.check_requirements)(\*modules, what[, extra])   | Raise [`MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency) unless every one of `modules` is installed.             |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`import_lazily`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.import_lazily)(name, \*, what[, extra])         | The module `name`, imported now; a failure to import it is a [`MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency). |
| [`missing_modules`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.missing_modules)(modules)                       | The `modules` that cannot be imported, found without importing them.                                                             |

### Exceptions

| [`MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency)(modules, \*, what[, extra])   | A library an operation needs is not installed (the message says how to install it).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### annals.requirements.DFLT_EXTRA *= 'pdf'*

the extra of annals that installs everything a conversion may need

### *exception* annals.requirements.MissingDependency(modules, , what, extra='pdf')

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

A library an operation needs is not installed (the message says how to install it).

### annals.requirements.PACKAGES *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]* *= {'PIL': ('pillow', ''), 'markdown_it': ('markdown-it-py', ''), 'markdownify': ('markdownify', ''), 'pdfdol': ('pdfdol', ''), 'playwright': ('playwright', 'Then fetch its browser: playwright install chromium'), 'pypdf': ('pypdf', ''), 'weasyprint': ('weasyprint', 'It also needs the Pango library (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install libpango-1.0-0).')}*

module name -> (pip name, system hint or `""`)

### annals.requirements.check_requirements(\*modules, what, extra='pdf')

Raise [`MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency) unless every one of `modules` is installed.

Cheap (nothing is imported), so a caller checks everything a job will use *before* it
starts, and fails at once instead of half way.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### annals.requirements.import_lazily(name, , what, extra='pdf')

The module `name`, imported now; a failure to import it is a [`MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency).

A library that is installed but cannot load (WeasyPrint without Pango raises
`OSError`) is reported the same way.

### annals.requirements.missing_modules(modules)

The `modules` that cannot be imported, found without importing them.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/annals.search.html.md

# annals.search

How the catalog answers a query: the search strategies.

A strategy is a callable `(query, rows, text_of) -> rows`: given every listed row (the
catalog has already listed them and overlaid the owner’s tags) and a way to get an item’s
full text, it returns the rows that match, best first, each with a `snippet` of the
text around the match and, when it ranks, a `score` (higher is better). The catalog
takes one as its `search` keyword ([`annals.catalog.Catalog`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog)), so a smarter one
(semantic, hybrid, an agent that rewrites the query) plugs in at the same place.

Two ship here:

* [`IndexedSearch`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.IndexedSearch), the default when the data root is on this machine: a SQLite
  FTS5 index kept on disk (`cache/search/index.sqlite` under the data root). Each query
  brings it up to date first, re-reading only items whose stamp changed (their listed
  fields, and the `stamp` a source gives, else their time and size),
  so the first query after a restart costs one pass over the texts and every later one a
  few milliseconds. Matching is by word prefix with English stemming (`rate` finds
  “rates” and “rated”, not “separate”), every word required, ranked by BM25 with the
  title weighted most.
* [`scan_search()`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.scan_search), the index-free fallback (a remote data root, tests): every word
  must appear as a substring of the title, tags, session, excerpt, id or full text;
  newest first, as listed.

### Module Attributes

| [`SNIPPET_CHARS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SNIPPET_CHARS)   | characters of context on each side of the first match, in a snippet                  |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SNIPPET_TOKENS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SNIPPET_TOKENS)  | tokens in an index snippet (FTS5's own window)                                       |
| [`SNIPPET_ROWS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SNIPPET_ROWS)    | the best rows that get a snippet (each costs ~5 ms); the rest show their excerpt.    |
| [`MAX_RESULTS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.MAX_RESULTS)     | the most rows a ranked query returns; the page shows a few dozen at a time           |
| [`DFLT_WEIGHTS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.DFLT_WEIGHTS)    | column weights for BM25, in the order of `_COLUMNS` (the title matters most)         |
| [`INDEX_DIR`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.INDEX_DIR)       | where index files live, under the data root (`<name>.sqlite`)                        |
| [`SCHEMA_VERSION`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SCHEMA_VERSION)  | an old index is rebuilt                                                              |
| [`WINDOW_CHARS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.WINDOW_CHARS)    | characters of the body kept around the match for rows past `snippet_rows`            |
| [`SYNC_BATCH`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SYNC_BATCH)      | rows indexed per write transaction, so a first build never holds the lock for long   |
| [`SQL_VARS`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SQL_VARS)        | bound variables per statement (SQLite's default limit is far above; this stays safe) |

### Functions

| [`default_search`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.default_search)(data_root, \*[, name])    | The index `<data root>/cache/search/<name>.sqlite` when the data root is on this machine, else the scan.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`fts_query`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.fts_query)(q)                             | A user's words as an FTS5 query: every word required, each a prefix.                                       |
| [`query_words`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.query_words)(q)                           | The words of a query, lowercased: `"Data  Rates"` -> `["data", "rates"]`.                                  |
| [`scan_search`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.scan_search)(query, rows, text_of)        | Every word a substring of the row's fields or full text; rows kept in their order.                         |
| [`snippet_around`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.snippet_around)(text, words, \*[, width]) | The text around the first occurrence of any of `words`, on one line.                                       |

### Classes

| [`IndexedSearch`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.IndexedSearch)([path, weights, max_results, ...])   | A SQLite FTS5 index of every row's fields and text, synced per query by stamp.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SearchStrategy`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SearchStrategy)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)                 | `(query, rows, text_of) -> matching rows, best first`.                           |

### annals.search.DFLT_WEIGHTS *= (10.0, 5.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0)*

column weights for BM25, in the order of `_COLUMNS` (the title matters most)

### annals.search.INDEX_DIR *= 'cache/search'*

where index files live, under the data root (`<name>.sqlite`)

### *class* annals.search.IndexedSearch(path=':memory:', , weights=(10.0, 5.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0), max_results=500, snippet_tokens=24, snippet_rows=60)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A SQLite FTS5 index of every row’s fields and text, synced per query by stamp.

`path` is the index file (made on first use; `":memory:"` keeps it in memory).
`weights` are BM25’s per-column weights (title, tags, session/id/source, excerpt,
text). `max_results` caps a ranked answer; the best `snippet_rows` carry FTS5’s
snippet, the rest a cheaper window of text around the query’s longest word. Safe
across threads (one sync at a time: queries that arrive during a sync wait for it
rather than redo it) and across processes sharing the file (two web workers): every
write is one short `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. If the index fails (a locked or
damaged file), a query falls back to [`scan_search()`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.scan_search) rather than fail.

#### forget(key)

Drop an item from the index (it is gone for good).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### sync(rows, text_of)

(Re)index the rows whose stamp changed; returns how many.

Nothing is dropped here: a query only ever answers with the rows it was given, so
an item listed elsewhere (in the bin, behind a hiding store, or gone) simply does
not come back. [`forget()`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.IndexedSearch.forget) drops an item for good.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### annals.search.MAX_RESULTS *= 500*

the most rows a ranked query returns; the page shows a few dozen at a time

### annals.search.SCHEMA_VERSION *= '3'*

an old index is rebuilt

* **Type:**
  bumped when the schema or what is indexed changes

### annals.search.SNIPPET_CHARS *= 90*

characters of context on each side of the first match, in a snippet

### annals.search.SNIPPET_ROWS *= 60*

the best rows that get a snippet (each costs ~5 ms); the rest show their excerpt.
One page of the list (the page’s `LIST_PAGE`).

### annals.search.SNIPPET_TOKENS *= 24*

tokens in an index snippet (FTS5’s own window)

### annals.search.SQL_VARS *= 500*

bound variables per statement (SQLite’s default limit is far above; this stays safe)

### annals.search.SYNC_BATCH *= 200*

rows indexed per write transaction, so a first build never holds the lock for long

### *class* annals.search.SearchStrategy(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

`(query, rows, text_of) -> matching rows, best first`.

`rows` are what the reader may see (a strategy never answers with anything else);
`text_of(row)` reads an item’s full text. A strategy that keeps state about items
may also have `forget(key)`, which the catalog calls when an item is gone for good.

### annals.search.WINDOW_CHARS *= 90*

characters of the body kept around the match for rows past `snippet_rows`

### annals.search.default_search(data_root, , name='index')

The index `<data root>/cache/search/<name>.sqlite` when the data root is on this
machine, else the scan.

* **Return type:**
  [`SearchStrategy`](_autosummary/annals.search.html.md#annals.search.SearchStrategy)

### annals.search.fts_query(q)

A user’s words as an FTS5 query: every word required, each a prefix.

Each word is quoted, so FTS5 syntax typed by the user (`AND`, `-`, `:`, quotes)
is searched for as text, never run as an operator. Control characters are dropped,
and so is a word with no letter or digit (the tokenizer would drop it anyway, and an
empty phrase matches nothing), so a query of only punctuation is no query.

```pycon
>>> fts_query('data rates')
'"data"* "rates"*'
>>> fts_query('a"b NOT')
'"a""b"* "not"*'
>>> fts_query('  ... - *')
''
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.search.query_words(q)

The words of a query, lowercased: `"Data  Rates"` -> `["data", "rates"]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### annals.search.scan_search(query, rows, text_of)

Every word a substring of the row’s fields or full text; rows kept in their order.

The full text is read only for rows whose fields lack a word.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### annals.search.snippet_around(text, words, , width=90)

The text around the first occurrence of any of `words`, on one line.

```pycon
>>> snippet_around("alpha beta gamma", ["beta"], width=6)
'alpha beta g…'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md

# annals.sessions

The sessions that made a document: each one’s name and the link that opens it.

A document’s meta carries them as `sessions`, a list of `{"name": ..., "url": ...}`
in the order they first worked on it: the session that published it, then each session
that published a new version (`annals publish --replace`). A group shows the sessions of
its documents. The link is a claude.ai link (`https://claude.ai/code/<bridge session id>`),
which only the owner can open; it is provenance, like `source` and `artifact`, so it is
never part of the document’s own content and leaves with the meta: a share or a room shows
an allowlist of meta fields that does not name it.

```pycon
>>> sessions_of({"source": {"session": "b2", "session_url": "https://claude.ai/code/session_01X"}})
[{'name': 'b2', 'url': 'https://claude.ai/code/session_01X'}]
>>> merged_sessions([{"name": "a", "url": ""}], [{"name": "a", "url": "https://claude.ai/code/s"}, {"name": "b", "url": ""}])
[{'name': 'a', 'url': 'https://claude.ai/code/s'}, {'name': 'b', 'url': ''}]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`SESSION_URL_TEMPLATE`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.SESSION_URL_TEMPLATE)   | the claude.ai link of a session, from its Remote Control (bridge) session id                                           |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`BRIDGE_ENV_VAR`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.BRIDGE_ENV_VAR)         | its Remote Control session id                                                                                          |
| [`MAX_SESSIONS`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.MAX_SESSIONS)           | the first, and the latest ones (a living page republished by a new session every day would otherwise grow without end) |
| [`MAX_READ`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.MAX_READ)               | the most entries read from a meta written elsewhere, before merging                                                    |

### Functions

| [`checked_sessions`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.checked_sessions)(sessions, check_url)      | `sessions` with each link `check_url` refuses (it raises `ValueError`) emptied: a meta written by another publisher is checked again before a page shows its links.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`merged_sessions`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.merged_sessions)(\*lists[, limit])          | The sessions of `lists` in order, one entry each: the same link, or the same name when one of the two has no link, is the same session (the link is kept).            |
| [`session_names`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.session_names)(meta)                        | The names of the sessions that made `meta`'s document (for `ls --session`).                                                                                           |
| [`session_url_from_env`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.session_url_from_env)([env, var, template]) | The claude.ai link of the Claude Code session this process runs in, or `""`.                                                                                          |
| [`sessions_of`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#annals.sessions.sessions_of)(meta)                          | The sessions that made the document `meta` describes (see the module doc).                                                                                            |

# _autosummary/annals.share.html.md

# annals.share

Share links: one document (or a group) behind a public, unguessable, revocable link.

A share is a record under the data root, `shares/<token>.json`, written through the
same [`annals.target.Target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target) as the documents, so `annals share` works over ssh
exactly like `annals publish`. The record is the whole contract; the owner’s API, the
page’s Share button, the CLI and the public share server (`annals.share_api`) are
surfaces over it:

```default
{
 "token": "<22 url-safe chars, 128 random bits>",
 "title": "...", "created": "<iso>",
 "root": {"kind": "doc" | "group", "id": "<id>"},
 "docs": {"<doc id>": ["<file>", ...], ...},   # what the link may reach, and only that
 "expires": "<iso>" | null,
 "password": "scrypt$..." | null,               # a hash; the password is never stored
 "revoked": "<iso>" | null                       # a tombstone: a revoked link is a 404
}
```

`docs` is the scope. Every request of the public server is checked against it, never
against what the link was made from: a file not listed is a 404 even when it sits beside
the shared page, and a page or a link of the shared text that points outside the scope is
removed before the text leaves the server ([`filter_refs()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.filter_refs)), so the recipient sees
neither private ids nor private paths.

The link itself (the token, the password gate, expiry, revocation) is a
`caplinks.CapabilityLinks` over these records; what is annals’ own is the scope
and the filtering. The password is a gate on the link, not an account: anyone who knows
both may read. It is hashed (stdlib `scrypt` by default, the `hasher` seam takes
argon2), and a correct one earns an HMAC cookie keyed by that hash, so changing the
password or revoking the link ends every open session.

| [`ANNALS_ID`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.ANNALS_ID)   | an annals id (doc or group) as [`annals.store.mk_id()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.mk_id) makes them   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`references`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.references)(text, kind, \*[, from_dir])            | What a page points at: files of its document, and annals pages (by id).                                                                                                                                                |
