### Classes

| [`Shares`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.Shares)(store, \*[, hasher, clock])   | Create, read, list and revoke shares of a `DocStore`'s documents.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### annals.share.ANNALS_ID *= '\\\\d{8}-\\\\d{6}-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)\*'*

an annals id (doc or group) as [`annals.store.mk_id()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.mk_id) makes them

### *class* annals.share.Shares(store, \*, hasher=None, clock=<function now_utc>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Create, read, list and revoke shares of a `DocStore`’s documents.

What a share reaches (its scope) is decided here; the link itself is `links`, a
`caplinks.CapabilityLinks` over the records under `shares/`. `hasher`
hashes link passwords (stdlib scrypt by default); `clock` returns the current UTC
`datetime` (tests pin it).

#### check_password(record, password)

Whether `password` opens `record`.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### create(ref, , include=None, exclude=(), password=None, expires='7d', title=None, files_of=None)

Share a document or a group (`ref` is its id); return the record (no hash).

A document is shared with all its files unless `include` names some (the page
itself always goes); `include` may also name annals pages the document links
to, which then open inside the share. A group is shared with all its documents
unless `include` names some. `exclude` removes files (or a group’s documents).
A linked page goes with the files it shows. `expires` is anything
`parse_expires()` reads, 7 days by default (`"never"` for none); `password`
gates the link (at least `caplinks.MIN_PASSWORD_LEN` characters).
`files_of(meta)` narrows which files of each of a group’s documents go (all of
them by default; [`annals.notebook.source_scope()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_scope) keeps only the pages and
what they show).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### included(record)

`(meta, files)` for each document of a share still there, in the share’s order.

`files` are the document’s files the share includes; a document deleted or in
the bin since the link was made is left out.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.Shares.list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict), [`list`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.Shares.list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]

#### list(, all=False)

Every share, newest first, without hashes; `all` adds revoked and expired.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.Shares.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### record(token)

The stored record (hash included), revoked or not; `None` if there is none.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### resources(doc_id)

What the Share dialog offers for a document: its files, and the pages it links.

`{"main", "files": [{"rel", "kind", "size", "referenced"}], "pages": [{"id",
"title", "kind"}]}`. `referenced` marks the files the page itself shows or
links; `pages` are the other annals documents its text links to.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### revoke(token)

End a link now (idempotent). The record stays, as a tombstone, for the list.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### status(token)

`("ok" | "expired" | "missing", record)`; a revoked link is `missing`.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

#### unlock_value(record)

The cookie value a correct password earns.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### unlocked(record, value, , max_age_s)

Whether a cookie value is a live unlock of this record (no password: always).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### annals.share.annals_urls(text)

The absolute links to annals document and group pages in `text`, once each, in order.

Any host: which annals a link belongs to is the reader’s config to decide
([`annals.config.link_target()`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.link_target)). Relative links (`../d/<id>`) are not found:
a document’s own links to its annals are absolute, as `annals publish` prints them.

```pycon
>>> annals_urls("see **[map](https://a.example.io/annals/d/20261119-075018-the-map-4a58)**, "
...             "<https://b.example.com/annals/g/20261117-163049-set?f=x> and "
...             "https://a.example.io/annals/d/20261119-075018-the-map-4a58 again")
['https://a.example.io/annals/d/20261119-075018-the-map-4a58', 'https://b.example.com/annals/g/20261117-163049-set']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### annals.share.dir_of(rel)

The directory part of a relative path, with its trailing slash (`""` at the top).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.share.filter_refs(text, kind, , files, shared, from_dir='', private_hosts=())

`text` with every reference outside the share removed (or rewritten).

`files` are the document’s files the share includes; `shared(id)` maps an annals
id to where the recipient opens it (in scope) or `None` (not shared). A markdown
image out of scope disappears, a link keeps its words; an html attribute goes; a bare
annals url becomes “(link not shared)” and a bare annals id “(not shared)”. The text
of the page itself is the owner’s: only references are touched. An absolute url on
one of `private_hosts` (the owner’s own) goes too, whatever its path. Every kind of
text is filtered (markdown, html, plain text, svg): only markdown syntax is markdown’s.
Best effort by design, and the second line of defence: the share server answers 404
for anything outside the share however the text names it.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.share.ref_decider(, from_dir, files, shared, private_hosts=())

`url -> new url` (often the same) or `None` (remove it).

The one rule of what a shared text may point at; [`filter_refs()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.filter_refs) applies it to
the references it finds in text, [`annals.notebook`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#module-annals.notebook) to a rendered page’s links.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### annals.share.references(text, kind, , from_dir='')

What a page points at: files of its document, and annals pages (by id).

`{"files": [rel, ...], "ids": [annals id, ...]}`, each in first-seen order; it
feeds the Share dialog, which offers them to the owner.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.share.remove_unshared_ids(text, shared)

`text` with every annals id that `shared` does not map replaced by a marker.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

A relative url as a file path inside the document, or `None` if it is not one.

```pycon
>>> resolve_rel("img/a.png?x=1#y", "notes/")
'notes/img/a.png'
```

# _autosummary/annals.share_page.html.md

# annals.share_page

A share link’s page with its text in it, and no script, so every reader can read it.

A share link used to answer with a shell: a `<title>` and an empty `<div>` that the
viewer’s script filled, with an html document inside a frame. NotebookLM made a
twenty-minute audio overview of such a link’s title. Its fetcher does run script, so it saw
the viewer’s buttons, but a group shows only titles there and a frame is not read. So the
page a link opens is now the shared text itself, rendered on the server under the rules
every shared text already follows, and nothing on it runs. The owner asked for exactly that:
a person only needs the document. The script viewer (galleries, players, downloads) is one
link away, `<link>/?viewer`.

The same share also answers as one Markdown file and one PDF, with the same token, expiry
and revocation (the routes are `annals.share_api`’s); the page names them in
`<link rel="alternate">` and in a line at its top:

```default
<link>/                 the page: every shared document's text (a group's, in order)
<link>/d/<id>           the page of one document of the share
<link>/share.md         the whole share as one Markdown file
<link>/share.pdf        the whole share as one PDF (images included)
<link>/d/<id>.md|.pdf   one document of it
<link>/?viewer          the script viewer, as before
```

What goes in the page, per document: its markdown and html files (the notebook sources of
[`annals.notebook`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#module-annals.notebook), numbered files first), markdown rendered with links and images
made safe by [`annals.notebook.render_source_body()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.render_source_body), html reduced to its structure and
words by [`annals.combine.html_body()`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.html_body) with a link to the page as designed; for a
document with no text, its images; its audio and video with the browser’s own players;
then links to its other files. Past [`STATIC_MAX_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.share_page.html.md#annals.share_page.STATIC_MAX_BYTES) of text or
[`STATIC_MAX_FILES`](_autosummary/annals.share_page.html.md#annals.share_page.STATIC_MAX_FILES) files, the remaining files and documents are links to their own pages, so a large group still answers quickly and every
document stays reachable. A document that *is* an html page ([`designed_page()`](_autosummary/annals.share_page.html.md#annals.share_page.designed_page)) is
served as itself at its own link, filtered and sandboxed as `/raw` serves it, with a
`<base>` ([`with_base()`](_autosummary/annals.share_page.html.md#annals.share_page.with_base)) so its images and styles load.

`page` with `<base href>` as its first element, so its relative references

# _autosummary/annals.sources.html.md

# annals.sources

Item sources: everything the page lists, wherever it lives, as rows of one shape.

A *source* is a named, read-mostly collection of items. Two kinds exist:

* [`PublishedSource`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.PublishedSource): the documents agents published (a [`annals.store.DocStore`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore)).
* [`FolderSource`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.FolderSource): a folder of files owned by someone else, read in place and never
  written (the crowsnest ledgers, and any other personal folder later). Its items are the
  folder’s files, keyed by their path relative to the folder.

Every source yields the same row shape, which the page lists, searches and filters:

`key`      `<source>:<id>`, unique across sources (the API’s item id)
`source`   the source’s name; `id` the item’s id within it
`title`, `kind` (see [`annals.store.kind_of()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.kind_of)), `session` (who wrote it)
`time`     ISO 8601, UTC: publication time, or a file’s last modification
`size`, `tags` (the item’s own; the catalog overlays the owner’s), `excerpt`

Sources are plain objects with a few methods (the [`Source`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.Source) protocol), so a new kind
of folder is a new class or a new keyword argument, never a change to the API.

### Module Attributes

| [`SOURCE_NAME_RE`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.SOURCE_NAME_RE)        | a source name is a url segment and part of every item key                            |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`RESERVED_SOURCE_NAMES`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.RESERVED_SOURCE_NAMES) | names the page uses for its own routes (`/all`, `/trash`) or the published documents |

### Functions

| `iso_utc`(ts)                                                             |                                                                                                                                     |

### *class* annals.sources.FolderSource(root, \*, name, title=None, exclude=('.\*', '_\_pycache_\_', '\*.pyc', '\*.pyo'), session_of=<function top_level_name>)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

A folder of files, read in place and never written, as a `Mapping` of rows.

Keys are paths relative to `root` (`"annals.md"`, `"cw-liaise/design.md"`), values
listing rows. The folder is walked on every listing (a stat per file, cheap for
hundreds), and a file is re-read only when its size or mtime changed. Hidden files and
caches are skipped (`exclude`, the same patterns a directory publish skips), and so
is anything that resolves outside `root`.

`session_of(rel)` names who wrote a file; the default suits a folder of per-session
files and sub-folders ([`top_level_name()`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#annals.sources.top_level_name)).

#### file_path(rel)

The file on disk; `KeyError` if it is absent, hidden, or escapes the root.

Only the canonical spelling of a path is accepted (`a/b.md`, not `./a/b.md`,
`a//b.md` or `a/b.md/`), so one file has one key.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

#### text(rel)

The file’s text (cached until it changes); `""` for binaries and huge files.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# _autosummary/annals.store.html.md

# annals.store

The document store: a flat set of documents, tags, groups and a recycle bin, as plain files.

Layout under the data root (local or remote, see [`annals.target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#module-annals.target)):

```default
docs/<id>/meta.json         one document: metadata
docs/<id>/<main file>       its content (index.html, report.md, ...), plus any assets
docs/<id>/.versions/<n>/    an earlier version, whole (its own meta.json and files)
docs/<id>.r<stamp>-<hex>/   a replacement not applied yet (``publish(replace=<id>)``)
trash/<id>/...              the same shape; the recycle bin is a move
groups/<gid>.json           a named, ordered list of document ids with its own URL
```

Flat on purpose: agents from many corpora do not share a hierarchy, and every placement
decision costs tokens. Tags and groups carry the structure. Ids are time-sortable and
readable (`20261003-203301-starwars-theme-report-3f9a`), so a listing is already in
publication order and a URL says what it points to.

Plain files, written whole, because the same tree is written by rsync from another machine
and read by the server; there is no index to keep consistent.

Living documents (one link that stays current) are a replace: the new files are written as
a *pending* replacement next to the document, never over it, and whoever reads the store
applies it ([`DocStore.settle()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.settle)): the current files move under `.versions/<n>/` and
the replacement takes the id. Writing beside rather than over is what lets a replace travel
through an outbox (a directory another machine pulls and empties): the pending directory is
just another new directory to pull, and the store on the reading side applies it. Applying
is a sequence of renames, each claimed atomically, so two readers never apply the same
replacement twice and nothing is ever deleted.

  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### list(, trash=False)

Every document’s meta, last changed first (`updated`, else `created`).

Pending replacements are applied first (when this store settles). One whose
document is not here is listed under its own id, so it is never out of sight.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### make_group(title, doc_ids, , gid=None, live_only=True)

Create (or overwrite) a group: a titled, ordered list of documents.

The title is cleaned (control characters dropped, whitespace collapsed, at most
`MAX_GROUP_TITLE` long, not blank); repeats are dropped, keeping the first; each
document must exist and not be in the bin unless `live_only=False` (a bundle that
keeps a document later binned). `ValueError` says which rule failed. An explicit
`gid` rewrites that group, under its lock.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### meta(doc_id, , settle=True)

One document’s meta; `in_trash` says which side of the bin it is on.

`<id>@<n>` is version `n`: its own meta, with `version_of` naming the document.
A pending replacement, read by its own id, says `pending`. `settle=False`
skips applying pending replacements (for a hot path such as a raw file).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### pending(doc_id=None, , names=None)

Pending replacements (directory names), oldest first; of one document if given.

`names`: the listing of `docs/` when the caller already has it.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### publish(\*sources, title=None, tags=(), source=None, text=None, filename='document.md', exclude=('.\*', '_\_pycache_\_', '\*.pyc', '\*.pyo'), replace=None, artifact=None, pdf=True, pdf_renderer='default')

Publish files (or a directory, or `text`) as ONE document; return its meta.

One markdown or html file is the common case. A directory is published whole, with
`index.html` (or the first renderable file) as the page shown. `text` publishes a
string as `filename` instead of reading sources. `exclude` lists glob patterns
skipped inside a directory (hidden files and caches by default; `()` keeps all).

`replace` (a document id) publishes a new version of that document instead of a
new document: same id, same link, the current files kept as a version. It is
written as a pending replacement and applied at once when this store settles
(otherwise where the store is read). The returned meta says `pending` until then.

`artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link, see [`check_artifact_url()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.check_artifact_url)) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page links out to it. A
replacement that names none keeps the document’s current one.

An html page gets its own Download PDF button, and `<stem>.pdf` printed beside
it by `pdf_renderer` unless it has one ([`annals.pagepdf`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#module-annals.pagepdf), which says how a
page declares or opts out). `pdf=False` leaves the page as it is.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### purge(doc_id)

Delete a document that is in the bin. Refuses one that is not.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### read_text(doc_id, rel=None)

A document’s main file (or one of its files) as text.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### rename(doc_id, title)

Give a document a title of the owner’s choosing; a later version keeps it.

The title is cleaned as a group’s is ([`clean_title()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.clean_title)). A version or a pending
replacement is refused (rename the document). Works in the bin too. Only `title`
and `renamed` change in the stored meta, which is read again under the document’s
lock: a document that moved meanwhile (trashed, restored, purged) is a
`RuntimeError`, never a meta written where its files are not. Returns its meta.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### rename_group(gid, title)

Give a group a new title (cleaned as at creation); its documents stay as they are.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Move a document out of the bin (idempotent).

  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Case-insensitive match of every query word against title, tags, excerpt, source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### settle(doc_id=None)

Apply pending replacements (of one document, or all); return the ids replaced.

A replacement whose document is not here yet (it is still on its way, or the
document was purged) stays pending and is listed under its own id.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore.list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### trash(doc_id)

### *class* annals.store.HidingStore(store, , hide)

Bases: [`DocStore`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.DocStore)

The documents of `store` without those `hide(meta)` is true of, on the same target.

A hidden document is absent, not refused: it is not listed or found, [`meta()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.HidingStore.meta) raises
`KeyError` for it, its versions and its pending replacements (so whatever reads a
document through the store, its page, files, versions or a share, answers as for a
missing one), and groups read through this store leave it out. An API built over this
store therefore cannot show it anywhere, whichever route asks; [`hides()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.HidingStore.hides) lets what
keeps records of its own about documents (shares) hide those records too. Reads go
through `store`, so a subclass’s reading still applies; writes reach the same target,
and a group is always rewritten from its whole list, so hiding never deletes anything.

# _autosummary/annals.tables.html.md

# annals.tables

Scrolling, zooming tables for published html pages.

A published html page is served as written; this adds one inlined script (the page’s own
`ui/tables.js`) that wraps each data table in a horizontally scrollable, zoomable box,
and lifts a viewport meta that forbids pinch-zoom. Markdown documents get the same script
from the page itself, so both paths share one implementation.

### Functions

| [`add_table_tools`](_autosummary/annals.tables.html.md#annals.tables.add_table_tools)(html)   | `html` with the table script injected, unless it has no table or opts out.                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`allow_zoom`](_autosummary/annals.tables.html.md#annals.tables.allow_zoom)(html)        | `html` with pinch-zoom allowed: no `user-scalable=no` or scale limits in its viewport meta.                         |
| [`tables_version`](_autosummary/annals.tables.html.md#annals.tables.tables_version)()        | A short hash of what [`add_table_tools()`](_autosummary/annals.tables.html.md#annals.tables.add_table_tools) injects, for a page's ETag. |

### annals.tables.add_table_tools(html)

`html` with the table script injected, unless it has no table or opts out.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### annals.tables.allow_zoom(html)

`html` with pinch-zoom allowed: no `user-scalable=no` or scale limits in its viewport meta.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### annals.tables.tables_version()

A short hash of what [`add_table_tools()`](_autosummary/annals.tables.html.md#annals.tables.add_table_tools) injects, for a page’s ETag.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/annals.tags.html.md

# annals.tags

The owner’s tags: a `MutableMapping` from item key to tag list, kept apart from the items.

Tags the owner adds on the page are stored here, never in the items themselves: a folder
source belongs to whoever writes it (a crowsnest ledger belongs to its session), so annals
must not edit it, and a published document’s `meta.json` is the publisher’s record.
An entry, once present, is the item’s whole tag list (it replaces the item’s own tags, so
removing a tag the publisher set works too); deleting the entry falls back to them.

[`JsonTagStore`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#annals.tags.JsonTagStore), the default, is one JSON file under the data root
(`<data root>/tags/tags.json`), written atomically. Any `MutableMapping[str, list[str]]`
can replace it (`mk_api(tags=...)`), e.g. a table in a database.

### Functions

| [`normalize_tags`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#annals.tags.normalize_tags)(tags)   | Trimmed, single-spaced, de-duplicated (ignoring case), sorted; refuses junk.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`JsonTagStore`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#annals.tags.JsonTagStore)(path)   | `{item key: [tags]}` in one JSON file (see [`annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore)).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* annals.tags.JsonTagStore(path)

Bases: [`JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore)

`{item key: [tags]}` in one JSON file (see [`annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore)).

Safe with several server processes on one machine; a damaged file reads as empty and is
kept aside (`tags.json.damaged`) at the next write.

#### clean(value)

The value as stored; raise `ValueError` to refuse it.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### valid(value)

Whether a value read from the file is kept (an invalid one is logged and skipped).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### annals.tags.normalize_tags(tags)

Trimmed, single-spaced, de-duplicated (ignoring case), sorted; refuses junk.

Raises `ValueError` for a tag that is not a string, is longer than `MAX_TAG_LEN`,
holds control characters, or for more than `MAX_TAGS_PER_ITEM` tags.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/annals.target.html.md

# annals.target

The transport seam: a document tree lands in a directory, here or on another machine.

A `Target` is the handful of filesystem verbs the store needs (put a directory, move,
remove, read and write a text file, list sub-directories, read every `meta.json` under a
directory). Two implementations:

* [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget): a directory on this machine, plain `pathlib`/`shutil`.
* [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget): `host:path` on another machine, through the system `ssh` and
  `rsync` in batch mode (no prompts, so an agent never hangs). The host is whatever the
  user’s `~/.ssh/config` resolves, so an alias such as `tw` works.

[`parse_target()`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.parse_target) picks one from a string. An HTTP target (a bearer-token ingest
endpoint) is the declared replacement for the ssh one and is not built yet.

### Module Attributes

| [`RECORD_SEP`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.RECORD_SEP)   | Separator between concatenated meta.json files when reading many at once over ssh.                                                  |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`META_GLOB`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.META_GLOB)    | each document's meta.json                                                                                                           |
| [`LOCK_NOTE`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LOCK_NOTE)    | the note a lock directory is created with (see [`Target.make_lock()`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target.make_lock))                 |
| [`SSH_SHARE_S`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SSH_SHARE_S)  | the several calls of one command (and the next command soon after) reuse it instead of paying a handshake each (~3 s to a far host) |

### Functions

| [`check_glob`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.check_glob)(pattern)       | A glob safe to hand a remote shell unquoted: names, `*` and `/` only, no hidden part.                                                                             |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_rel`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.check_rel)(rel)            | Refuse anything that could escape the root; the store only ever passes safe paths.                                                                                |
| [`parse_target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.parse_target)(spec)        | `host:/path` becomes an [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget); anything else a [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget). |
| [`ssh_opts`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.ssh_opts)(\*[, share_dir]) | The ssh options: batch mode, and one connection shared by consecutive calls.                                                                                      |

### Classes

| [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget)(root)          | A directory on this machine.                                                |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget)(host, root)      | `host:path` on another machine, via the system ssh and rsync in batch mode. |
| [`Target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target)(\*args, \*\*kwargs) | What the store needs from wherever the documents live.                      |

the note a lock directory is created with (see [`Target.make_lock()`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target.make_lock))

### *class* annals.target.LocalTarget(root)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A directory on this machine.

`read_metas()` keeps each meta it parsed, keyed by its file’s inode, mtime, ctime
and size (every write replaces the file, so a new inode), and resolves the root once
per listing, not twice per file: listing a thousand documents costs a `stat` per
document, not a parse. It hands back copies, so a caller may change what it gets.

the several calls of one command

`host:/path` becomes an [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.SshTarget); anything else a [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.LocalTarget).

* **Return type:**
  [`Target`](_autosummary/annals.target.html.md#annals.target.Target)

### annals.target.ssh_opts(, share_dir=None)

The ssh options: batch mode, and one connection shared by consecutive calls.

The shared connection’s socket lives in `share_dir` (default `~/.ssh`); without that
directory every call opens its own connection, as plain `ssh` would.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]


# _autosummary/annals.titles.html.md

# annals.titles

A title for a file whose name says nothing: `overview.mp3`, `output.html`, `index.md`.

A document is titled by what it says (a `# heading`, a `<title>`), else by its file
name. Tools that make media often name every output the same (podpatch and hailing both
write `<folder>/overview.mp3`), so seven audio overviews were all titled “overview”. When
the file name is one of [`GENERIC_STEMS`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.GENERIC_STEMS), the title comes from beside the file
instead: the `title` of a JSON manifest in its folder ([`TITLE_FILES`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.TITLE_FILES)), else the
folder’s own name without its date and hash, but only when the folder was made by a tool
(its name carries a date stamp or a short hash): a person’s folder (their home, a repo, a
client’s) never names a document, since a title shows wherever the document is shared.

```pycon
>>> is_generic("overview") and is_generic("Final_Output") and not is_generic("theremin")
True
>>> folder_title("20261119-223540-theremin-and-gesture-controlled-7d32")
'theremin and gesture controlled'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`GENERIC_STEMS`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.GENERIC_STEMS)         | file names (without extension) that never title a document on their own       |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TITLE_FILES`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.TITLE_FILES)           | files a maker writes beside its output whose `title` names it, tried in order |
| [`MAX_TITLE`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.MAX_TITLE)             | the longest title taken from a manifest (a rename allows as much)             |
| [`UNINFORMATIVE_FOLDERS`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.UNINFORMATIVE_FOLDERS) | folder names that say nothing either (a title from one would be noise)        |

### Functions

| [`folder_title`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.folder_title)(name)              | A tool's output folder's name as a title: date stamp and trailing hash dropped, separators spaced; `""` for a folder no tool made (no stamp and no hash), or one whose words are only digits and hex (a uuid, a temporary folder's name).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_generic`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.is_generic)(stem, \*[, generic]) | Whether a file name (without extension) says nothing about what it holds: one of `generic`, or two of them ("final output", "audio overview").                                                                                              |
| [`title_beside`](_autosummary/annals.titles.html.md#annals.titles.title_beside)(path)              | A title for the file `path` from what is beside it (see the module doc), or `None` when its folder says nothing either.                                                                                                                     |

### annals.titles.GENERIC_STEMS *= frozenset({'audio', 'document', 'export', 'file', 'final', 'index', 'main', 'narration', 'out', 'output', 'overview', 'page', 'player', 'recording', 'render', 'report', 'result', 'speech', 'summary', 'take', 'track', 'untitled', 'video', 'voice'})*

file names (without extension) that never title a document on their own

### annals.titles.MAX_TITLE *= 200*

the longest title taken from a manifest (a rename allows as much)

### annals.titles.TITLE_FILES *= ('manifest.json', 'meta.json', 'script.json', 'info.json')*

files a maker writes beside its output whose `title` names it, tried in order

### annals.titles.UNINFORMATIVE_FOLDERS *= frozenset({'desktop', 'documents', 'downloads', 'home', 'overviews', 'root', 'scratchpad', 'temp', 'tmp', 'work'})*

folder names that say nothing either (a title from one would be noise)

### annals.titles.folder_title(name)

A tool’s output folder’s name as a title: date stamp and trailing hash dropped,
separators spaced; `""` for a folder no tool made (no stamp and no hash), or one whose
words are only digits and hex (a uuid, a temporary folder’s name).

```pycon
>>> folder_title("2026-11-22-tables-and-session-links"), folder_title("thorwhalen")
('tables and session links', '')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.titles.is_generic(stem, , generic=frozenset({'audio', 'desktop', 'document', 'documents', 'downloads', 'export', 'file', 'final', 'home', 'index', 'main', 'narration', 'out', 'output', 'overview', 'overviews', 'page', 'player', 'recording', 'render', 'report', 'result', 'root', 'scratchpad', 'speech', 'summary', 'take', 'temp', 'tmp', 'track', 'untitled', 'video', 'voice', 'work'}))

Whether a file name (without extension) says nothing about what it holds: one of
`generic`, or two of them (“final output”, “audio overview”).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### annals.titles.title_beside(path)

A title for the file `path` from what is beside it (see the module doc), or `None`
when its folder says nothing either.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "20261119-223540-theremin-7d32"; d.mkdir()
>>> title_beside(d / "overview.mp3")
'theremin'
>>> _ = (d / "manifest.json").write_text('{"title": "The Theremin: Invention, Spies"}')
>>> title_beside(d / "overview.mp3")
'The Theremin: Invention, Spies'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/annals.tools.html.md

# annals.tools

The operations, as plain functions: JSON-able arguments in, JSON-able dicts out.

This module is the single source of truth for what a annals can do. The CLI
(`annals.__main__`, via `cw`), the MCP server (`py2mcp` over string refs to these
names) and the shipped skill all describe the same functions, so there is nothing to keep
in parity. Nothing here prints or exits; the surfaces do that.

### Module Attributes

| [`LINK_CHECKED_SUFFIXES`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.LINK_CHECKED_SUFFIXES)   | the suffixes whose text the link check reads (prose an author writes by hand)                                               |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`LINKS_READ_SUFFIXES`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.LINKS_READ_SUFFIXES)     | the suffixes whose text [`show()`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.show) reads for the annals links a document makes |
| [`LINKS_MAX_FILES`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.LINKS_MAX_FILES)         | [`show()`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.show) reads at most this many of a document's text files for links ...    |
| [`LINKS_MAX_FILE_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.LINKS_MAX_FILE_BYTES)    |                                                                                                                             |
| [`EFFECTS`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.EFFECTS)                 | a surface serves the levels its caller allows.                                                                              |
| [`DFLT_EFFECTS`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.DFLT_EFFECTS)            | what an agent or a tool is offered unless its host asks for more (MCP reads this)                                           |

### Functions

| [`aggregate`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.aggregate)(group_id, \*[, format, output, ...])     | The files of a group (or one document) as ONE markdown, html or pdf file (nothing is stored).             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`configure`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.configure)(\*[, target, base_url, to, outbox, ...]) | Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.                            |
| [`copy`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.copy)(refs, \*, to[, source, target, base_url])     | Copy documents or groups to a named target, keeping their ids; print the new link.                        |
| [`export`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.export)(doc_id, \*[, format, file, output, ...])    | One markdown file of a document as a `.md` or a titled `.pdf`, as the page's Export gives it.             |
| [`group`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.group)(title, doc_ids, \*[, add_to, target, ...])   | Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.                                 |
| [`groups`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.groups)(\*[, target, base_url, to])                 | List groups, newest first.                                                                                |
| [`listen`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.listen)(doc_id, \*[, minutes, force, also, ...])    | Ask for a spoken overview of a document, as its page's Listen button does.                                |
| [`listen_down`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.listen_down)([reason, link, clear, target, to])     | Say why spoken overviews cannot be made, and where that is being fixed; or clear it.                      |
| [`listen_work`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.listen_work)(\*[, command, target, to])             | Fulfil the queued overview requests, one at a time (a timer runs this on the server).                     |
| [`ls`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.ls)([q, trash, limit, target, base_url, to, ...])   | List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.                           |
| [`overview_state`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.overview_state)(doc_id, \*[, target, to])           | Where a document's spoken overview stands (not asked for, queued, made, failed), without asking for one.  |
| [`page_shell`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.page_shell)(\*[, api, base, title])                 | The page's html shell, for a host that serves the API under its own prefix.                               |
| [`publish`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.publish)(paths, \*[, title, tags, group, ...])      | Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.                          |
| [`purge`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.purge)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                   | Delete documents that are in the bin for good (not restorable).                                           |
| [`references`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.references)(ref, \*[, form, also, target, to])      | The references of a document or a group, as its page's References action gives them.                      |
| [`rename`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.rename)(ref, title, \*[, target, to])               | Rename a document or a group (its link or id), as the page's Rename does.                                 |
| [`restore`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.restore)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                 | Bring documents back from the recycle bin.                                                                |
| [`serve`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.serve)(\*[, host, port, data_dir, base_path, ...])  | Serve the annals page and API (needs `pip install 'annals[server]'`).                                     |
| [`share`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.share)(ref, \*[, password, expires, include, ...])  | Make a public link to ONE document (or group) and print it; nothing else is reachable.                    |
| [`shareable`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.shareable)(doc_id, \*[, target, to])                | What the Share dialog offers for a document: its files, and the other annals documents its text links to. |
| [`shares`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.shares)(\*[, all, target, base_url, to])            | List share links, newest first (`all`: revoked and expired ones too).                                     |
| [`show`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.show)(doc_id, \*[, target, base_url, to])           | A document's metadata, link, the groups it is in, and the annals links in its text.                       |
| [`tag`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.tag)(doc_id, tags, \*[, target, to])                | Set a document's tags (comma separated; "" clears them), as the page's tag editor does.                   |
| [`tools_with`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.tools_with)([effects])                              | The operations whose effect is in `effects`, in the CLI's order: the list a caller-facing surface serves. |
| [`trash`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.trash)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                   | Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).                                                           |
| [`unshare`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.unshare)(links, \*[, target, to])                   | Revoke share links (their token or full link): they stop working at once.                                 |

### annals.tools.DFLT_EFFECTS *= frozenset({'read', 'write'})*

what an agent or a tool is offered unless its host asks for more (MCP reads this)

### annals.tools.EFFECTS *= {'aggregate': 'file', 'configure': 'write', 'copy': 'write', 'export': 'file', 'group': 'write', 'groups': 'read', 'listen': 'spend', 'listen_down': 'spend', 'listen_work': 'server', 'ls': 'read', 'overview_state': 'read', 'page_shell': 'server', 'publish': 'write', 'purge': 'destructive', 'references': 'read', 'rename': 'write', 'restore': 'write', 'serve': 'server', 'share': 'write', 'shareable': 'read', 'shares': 'read', 'show': 'read', 'tag': 'write', 'trash': 'write', 'unshare': 'write'}*

a surface serves the levels its caller
allows. `read` changes nothing; `write` changes the store or a setting and can be undone
or repeated; `file` writes a path on the machine that runs it; `destructive` cannot be
undone; `spend` costs money or queues work that does; `server` is run by a server or a
timer, never by a caller.

* **Type:**
  what a function does to the world, least to most

### annals.tools.LINKS_MAX_FILES *= 20*

[`show()`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.show) reads at most this many of a document’s text files for links …

### annals.tools.LINKS_MAX_FILE_BYTES *= 1000000*

… and none larger than this (bytes, from the document’s meta)

### annals.tools.LINKS_READ_SUFFIXES *= frozenset({'.htm', '.html', '.markdown', '.md', '.txt'})*

the suffixes whose text [`show()`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.show) reads for the annals links a document makes

### annals.tools.LINK_CHECKED_SUFFIXES *= frozenset({'.markdown', '.md', '.txt'})*

the suffixes whose text the link check reads (prose an author writes by hand)

### annals.tools.aggregate(group_id, , format='md', output=None, demote=1, order='numbered', no_toc=False, keep_wraps=False, target=None, to=None)

The files of a group (or one document) as ONE markdown, html or pdf file (nothing is stored).

`group_id` is a group’s or a document’s id or link. `format`: `md` (printed, or
written to `output`), `html` (a web page, the same) or `pdf` (needs `output`).
Markdown, html, text, PDF and image files go in; what cannot (audio, video, other
files, a damaged PDF) is listed on stderr, with the reason, and left out. The markdown
has the group’s title, a table of contents, then one `##` section per file named after
its path (a folder document’s files under its title). `order`: `numbered` puts paths
that start with a number first, numerically, the rest in the group’s order; `given`
keeps the group’s order. `demote` pushes each file’s headings that many levels down
(`0`: as written). Hard-wrapped lines are joined unless `keep_wraps`; `no_toc`
leaves out the table of contents. Redirect to save text, or name the file:
`annals aggregate <id> --format pdf --output bundle.pdf`. A PDF or html needs
`pip install 'annals[pdf]'`; a missing library says so.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.configure(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, outbox=False, share_base_url=None, room=False)

Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.

### Example

`annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals`.
`--to NAME` saves the target and base url as a named target (`annals publish --to NAME`)
and leaves the default alone. `--outbox` marks the target as an outbox: a directory
the server pulls and empties (it cannot be written to from here), so replacements are
left for the server to apply; it is kept by later changes (`ANNALS_OUTBOX=0` or an
edit of the file turns it off). `--share-base-url` is where share links point when
the share server is not at `<base-url>/shared` (a platform running it as its own
public app). `--room` marks a target an outside audience reads (a client’s room): what
is published or copied to it carries no provenance; kept by later changes, like
`--outbox`. With no arguments, shows the resolved settings without writing.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.copy(refs, , to, source=None, target=None, base_url=None)

Copy documents or groups to a named target, keeping their ids; print the new link.

`refs` are links (`https://.../annals/d/<id>`, `.../g/<group-id>`) or bare ids; only
the id is used, so the link may point at any instance. They are read from the default
target (or the named target `source`) and written to the named target `to`. A group
is copied with its documents and keeps its id and title. Copying again refreshes the
copy. The source must be readable from this machine (a directory, or `host:/path`).
`target`/`base_url` override the DESTINATION’s location, as in `publish`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.export(doc_id, , format='pdf', file=None, output=None, target=None, to=None)

One markdown file of a document as a `.md` or a titled `.pdf`, as the page’s Export gives it.

`file` names another markdown file of a folder document (default: the main one). A PDF
(images inside; needs the `annals[pdf]` extra) is a binary file, so name it with
`--output FILE`; `md` prints the text or writes it to `output`. For several documents
as one file, with a table of contents, use `annals aggregate`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.group(title, doc_ids, , add_to=None, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.

With `add_to` (a group id) the documents are added to that group instead, and `title`
is ignored. The documents must exist and not be in the bin; the title is cleaned (see
[`annals.store.clean_title()`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#annals.store.clean_title)).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.groups(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

List groups, newest first.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.listen(doc_id, , minutes=5, force=False, also=None, target=None, to=None)

Ask for a spoken overview of a document, as its page’s Listen button does. Spends money.

`also` (more document ids) asks for ONE overview of all of them together, as the page
does for a pick: their text is put in one document (made when the worker starts the job),
and the same documents at the same versions reuse it. `force` then does not apply.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.listen_down(reason='', , link='', clear=False, target=None, to=None)

Say why spoken overviews cannot be made, and where that is being fixed; or clear it.

With nothing given, shows the current state. The Audio tab then shows the reason and the
link instead of a Try again that cannot work, e.g.
`annals listen-down "the server's login expired" --link <issue url>`. The worker finds
out by itself too, and clears it on the next success; `--clear` clears it now and
queues every request that waited.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.listen_work(, command='', target=None, to=None)

Fulfil the queued overview requests, one at a time (a timer runs this on the server).

`command` makes one overview, with {source}, {minutes}, {out} and {url} filled in; by default,
`$ANNALS_OVERVIEW_COMMAND`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.ls(q='', , trash=False, limit=50, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, since=None, session=None, tag=None, meta=None)

List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.

`to` lists a named target instead of the default one. The rest are exact filters,
all of which must hold, for tools that poll: `since` (an ISO date or time, or an age
like `6h` or `2d`: published or replaced at or after it), `session` (the publishing session’s
name, whole, case-sensitive), `tag` (one tag, whole: the owner’s own tags, set by `annals tag`, win over the publisher’s) and `meta` (`key=value`,
several allowed, against the document’s `source`: `corpus=annals`). A row is
`{id, title, kind, tags, created, updated, source, url}`; with `--json` that is the contract
(`misc/docs/design.md`), and `total` counts the matches before `limit`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.overview_state(doc_id, , target=None, to=None)

Where a document’s spoken overview stands (not asked for, queued, made, failed), without asking for one.

Poll this after `annals listen`. For a combined overview (`listen --also`) give the
combined document’s id once the worker has made it; until then `listen` returns the state.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.page_shell(, api='/api/annals', base='/annals', title='annals')

The page’s html shell, for a host that serves the API under its own prefix.

An enlace app writes it once as its frontend:
`annals page-shell --api /api/annals --base /annals > frontend/index.html`.
The shell only names the two paths; the page’s code loads from the API, so it upgrades
with the package.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.tools.publish(paths, , title=None, tags='', group=None, add_to=None, session=None, session_url=None, all_files=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, replace=None, artifact=None, no_link_check=False, no_pdf=False, meta=None)

Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.

An audio or video file takes its timed text along as one document: `talk.mp3
talk.vtt talk.chapters.vtt` (or `talk.cues.json`) is one audio document whose page
shows the transcript and chapters (`annals.store.SIDECAR_SUFFIXES`).

`paths`: files of any kind (markdown, html, images, video, audio, pdf, text), a
directory (one document: an `index.html` or single page with its assets, else a
gallery of everything in it), or `-` for stdin (markdown). `tags` is comma separated. `group`
names a group to create from the published documents; the reply then carries
`group_url` too. `add_to` appends them to an existing group instead (its id, as
printed in a group link), so a second batch lands under the link the owner already has. `session` records who published (the source shown on the page), and `session_url`
the claude.ai link that opens that session; by default the link of the Claude Code session
this runs in (`CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`), `none` for no link. The document’s page
shows each session that made it, linked, under its title; a share or a room never does
([`annals.sessions`](_autosummary/annals.sessions.html.md#module-annals.sessions)). A directory skips
hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`) unless `all_files`.
`to` publishes to a named target of the config file (`[targets.NAME]`, see
`annals configure --to`) instead of the default one. `replace` (a document’s link or
id) publishes ONE path as a new version of that document: the link stays the same, the
page shows the new version and offers the earlier ones. That is how a living page (a
guide, a status page) keeps one link. `artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive
version” button. Publish the Artifact first, then the same page here with its link.
A markdown or text document that mentions an issue or a Slack/email/chat message
without linking to it gets a warning on stderr ([`annals.linkcheck`](_autosummary/annals.linkcheck.html.md#module-annals.linkcheck)); it is
published either way. `no_link_check` turns that check off.

An html page gets its own Download PDF button, inside the page, so it survives “open
full page”, raw links and shares, and `<stem>.pdf` printed beside it (headless
Chromium, the `pdf` extra; without it the button opens the print dialog). A page that
already has its PDF says so with `<link rel="alternate" type="application/pdf"
href="...">`; one with its own button marks it `data-annals-pdf`; `no_pdf` (or
`data-annals-pdf="off"` on `<html>`/`<body>`) leaves the page as it is
([`annals.pagepdf`](_autosummary/annals.pagepdf.html.md#module-annals.pagepdf)).

`meta` (`--meta key=value [key=value ...]`) records what the document belongs to, next
to `host`, `cwd` and `session` in its `source`: by convention `corpus` (the
repository or body of work), `repo`, `issue` (the issue it answers), `item` (a
desk item) and `kind` (report, brief, overview, render); other keys are kept as given.
`ls --session/--meta` finds them again. The CLI’s `--json` prints the result below
(`id`, `title`, `url`, and with a group `group_id` and `group_url`; several
paths give `docs`) as JSON and nothing else on stdout; that shape is a contract
(`misc/docs/design.md`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.purge(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Delete documents that are in the bin for good (not restorable). One that is not in the bin is refused.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.references(ref, , form='grouped', also=None, target=None, to=None)

The references of a document or a group, as its page’s References action gives them.

`ref` is a group’s or a document’s id or link. `form`: `grouped` (each document’s
references section as it is), `deduped` (every entry once, numbers removed) or `urls`
(one address per line, nothing else: what a notebook takes as pasted sources). Documents
with no references section are left out; none at all is an error. `also` (more document
ids) takes the references of those documents together, as a pick on the page does.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.tools.rename(ref, title, , target=None, to=None)

Rename a document or a group (its link or id), as the page’s Rename does.

The document keeps the owner’s title when a new version is published over it
(`publish --replace`). Returns `{id, title}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.restore(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Bring documents back from the recycle bin.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.serve(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8765, data_dir=None, base_path='/annals', allow_open=False, overviews=None)

Serve the annals page and API (needs `pip install 'annals[server]'`).

Auth comes from the environment: `ANNALS_WHOAMI_URL` + `ANNALS_ALLOWED_USERS` to sit
behind an existing login, `ANNALS_BASIC_USER` + `ANNALS_BASIC_PASSWORD` for HTTP Basic,
nothing for an open server on localhost. A host reachable beyond this machine with no auth
configured is refused unless `allow_open` (`--allow-open`) says something else gates it.
`overviews` (`--overviews '*'`, or reader names separated by commas) offers the Listen
button to those the login lets in (unset: `ANNALS_OVERVIEWS` decides, and unset it is
off; `--overviews ''` forces it off). It spends money, needs `ANNALS_OVERVIEW_COMMAND`
and a worker (`annals listen-work` on a timer), and a server with no login serves it
only on this machine.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### annals.tools.share(ref, , password=None, expires='7d', include=None, exclude=None, title=None, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

Make a public link to ONE document (or group) and print it; nothing else is reachable.

Returns three forms of the one link (the CLI prints the first on stdout, the others
on stderr): `url`, the page, whose text is in the html (a
person, NotebookLM or any fetcher reads it without running script); `markdown`, the
whole share as one text, for an agent; `pdf`, the same with its images. All three end
with the link’s expiry or revocation.

`ref` is a document or group id, or its link. The link opens without a login, shows
only that page and the files chosen, and can be revoked (`annals unshare`).
`include`: comma separated files of the document to share (the page itself always
is), or ids of other annals pages it links to; by default every file of the document
(for a group: every document; `include` then picks documents). `exclude` drops
files. `expires` (7 days unless told): `12h`, `30d`, `2w`, a date (`2026-11-01`,
through that day, UTC), an ISO time, or `never`. `password` gates the link (stored hashed; `-` reads it from
stdin, so it stays out of the shell history).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.shareable(doc_id, , target=None, to=None)

What the Share dialog offers for a document: its files, and the other annals documents its text links to.

`{main, files: [{rel, kind, size, referenced}], pages: [{id, title, kind}]}`: the
choices `annals share` takes for what a link may show.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.shares(, all=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

List share links, newest first (`all`: revoked and expired ones too).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.show(doc_id, , target=None, base_url=None, to=None)

A document’s metadata, link, the groups it is in, and the annals links in its text.

`doc_id` may be the document’s link, on any annals this machine is configured for: the
link finds its own place (`to` names one explicitly). A group’s link gives the group
and its documents’ links. `links` are the links to other annals documents and groups
found in the document’s text files, on any annals this machine can read: follow them
with `annals show` or `annals aggregate`. To read the text, use `annals aggregate <link>`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.tag(doc_id, tags, , target=None, to=None)

Set a document’s tags (comma separated; “” clears them), as the page’s tag editor does.

The tags are the owner’s overlay, kept apart from the document and shown by `ls` and
`show` in place of the publisher’s. They live where the documents do, so this refuses an
outbox or a remote target. `doc_id` may be the document’s link. Returns `{id, tags}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.tools_with(effects=frozenset({'read', 'write'}))

The operations whose effect is in `effects`, in the CLI’s order: the list a caller-facing surface serves.

```pycon
>>> [f.__name__ for f in tools_with({"read"})]
['ls', 'show', 'groups', 'references', 'shareable', 'shares', 'overview_state']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### annals.tools.trash(doc_ids, , target=None, to=None)

Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### annals.tools.unshare(links, , target=None, to=None)

Revoke share links (their token or full link): they stop working at once.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`annals` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `annals-publish`

Publish a document or media (a markdown report, an html page, images, video, audio, a PDF, or a whole folder of renders) to the owner’s private annals and hand back the link, so they can read it on a phone or tablet away from the terminal. Use whenever the user asks to “publish this”, “post it to my annals”, “put it where I can read it on my phone”, “give me a link to that report”, “show me the images”, “where can I see the renders”, “share the page with me”, or whenever you have produced a document longer than a few lines that the user will want to read later or elsewhere. Also covers living pages (one link that stays current: `--replace`), grouping several documents under one link, listing what is in the annals, and moving a document to the recycle bin. Also use whenever you are handed an annals link (`.../annals/d/<id>` or `.../annals/g/<id>`) to read: the page is private, so read it with `annals aggregate <link>`, never by fetching the URL and never by asking for a share link.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/annals annals-publish --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`annals/data/skills/annals-publish`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/annals/tree/HEAD/annals/data/skills/annals-publish) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install annals`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/annals/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`annals.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/annals/annals.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/annals/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
